lesson_title: Mid-Latitude Cyclones: The Storm Highway Over the South Coast
hook_text: One wind swing tells you a cold front just passed — learn the storm's signature in 60 seconds.
clip_script: During passage the change is compressed into an hour or two. The cold wedge arrives and hurls the warm-sector air upward; cumulonimbus erupts overhead; rain arrives in hard, cold bursts, with thunder possible and snow on the high peaks inland. And the wind vane performs the single most examinable move in this topic: the wind backs sharply around from north-west, through west, to south-west. That wind swing is the fingerprint of a frontal passage. Any answer describing a cold front that leaves it out is missing the front's signature.
visual_style: Split-screen over a Garden Route beachfront: flags snapping north-west, a black wall of cloud sliding in from the sea, sheets of rain, then crisp sunshine with snow on the Outeniquas — a compass needle swinging NW to SW stamped across each phase.
mood: Storm-chaser energy with a calm, confident payoff.
pacing: Fast build to the front's arrival, hard freeze-frame on the wind swing, cool clear finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and be able to draw all three stages before your final exams.
